content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3: lend one cross-skilled agent from payments to general 14:00-14:30 and delay general's 14:15-14:45 breaks by 15 minutes. Predicted service level is 98.4% for 13:45-15:45 at no extra cost.","why":"The morning spike was caused by the UPI switch outage (INC-20261006-6998). Payments calls hit 213 against 111.9 forecast at 10:30, service level fell to 4.7% and 59 calls were abandoned. Staffing is at plan (42 of 43) and handle time is below forecast, so this is a demand problem, not a staffing one. For the 13:45-15:45 window, every option is predicted well above the 80% target, including doing nothing (97.9%). P3 has the best prediction of the zero-cost options: 98.4% on both payments and general, 0.2% abandon rate, no policy violations and 99.1% for the rest of the day.","trade_offs":["P0 (no action) also costs nothing and is predicted at 97.9%, comfortably above target. P3 adds a small improvement in exchange for two minor changes on the floor.","P1 (full-hour agent move) is predicted at 98.0% and lowers the rest-of-day figure to 98.9%. P3's half-hour move takes less from payments and still lifts payments to 98.4%.","P2 (break delay only) is predicted at 98.2%. P3 adds the short move for a slightly better 98.4% and a 0.2% abandon rate.","None of the options cost anything extra, and none put the other queue at risk on these predictions."],"watch":"The gains over doing nothing are small, so the real risk is the UPI incident. If the switch fails again, payments volume could jump the way it did at 10:30. Track payments arrivals and the incident status. If volume climbs, bring the lent agent back to payments early and re-plan."}
